bull.b: The subscription-led model provides recurring revenue visibility through term contracts, renewals and expansion within existing accounts. A 98% renewal rate supports durable customer retention, while multi-product adoption can deepen relationships and increase lifetime account value over time.

bull.t: Sustained revenue growth and high gross margins
bull.b: Growth above 20% combined with an expected 81% subscription gross margin indicates strong software economics and meaningful operating leverage. These characteristics support continued investment in product development and sales while preserving the potential for durable profitability as scale increases.

Accelerating AI contract value and a repeatedly increased target show that AI is becoming a material growth engine rather than only a product feature. Broad adoption across IT, HR, security, CRM and creator workflows can expand ServiceNow’s addressable market and customer spend.

bear.b: The sharp increase in trailing-twelve-month debt adds financial exposure despite the company’s generally healthy balance sheet. Higher obligations can reduce flexibility for investment or acquisitions and make weaker operating performance more consequential if cash generation or margins deteriorate.

Lower trailing profitability suggests that operating costs or mix effects are absorbing part of the benefit from revenue growth. If margin compression persists, earnings and reinvestment capacity could lag the company’s strong top-line expansion, making execution on efficiency and scaling important.

Expected cRPO deceleration indicates that forward subscription momentum will moderate in the near term, even though management expects the related deals to contribute revenue. A higher on-premises mix and renewal timing can make reported backlog growth less representative of underlying demand.
